content: If you miss a dose of this medication, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular scheduled time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. This medication, neomycin, can rarely cause serious kidney problems and nerve damage, which may result in permanent hearing loss (including deafness or reduced hearing) and balance issues. These severe side effects can occur even in individuals without pre-existing kidney problems and while taking usual doses. Hearing problems may develop long after the medication has been discontinued. The risk is higher in older adults, those with kidney disease, or those experiencing severe dehydration. The risk also increases with higher doses or prolonged use of this medication. Your doctor will carefully monitor you, which may include hearing, kidney, and urine tests, to reduce the risk of these side effects. Avoid taking other medications that may increase the risk of these serious side effects when combined with neomycin (refer to the Drug Interactions section). Neomycin is used to reduce the risk of infection following certain intestinal surgeries. It belongs to a class of drugs known as aminoglycoside antibiotics. It may also be used alongside a special diet to treat a serious brain condition called hepatic encephalopathy, which is caused by an excess of ammonia in the body. Normally, the liver removes ammonia, but liver disease can lead to a buildup of this substance. This antibiotic treats only bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections (e.g., common cold, flu). To reduce the risk of infection after intestinal surgery, take this medication as directed by your doctor, usually for 3 or 4 doses the day before surgery. The dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. To minimize the risk of hearing loss and other side effects, take this medication at the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible duration. Do not increase your dose, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer time than prescribed. If you are taking this medication for hepatic encephalopathy, take it at evenly spaced intervals for optimal effect. To help you remember, take it at the same times each day. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking neomycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other aminoglycoside antibiotics (e.g., tobramycin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. High doses or prolonged use of neomycin may impair your body’s ability to absorb certain foods, nutrients (e.g., iron, vitamins A and B-12), and drugs (e.g., digoxin, warfarin). Neomycin may also reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). This medication is not recommended for use during pregnancy. Although there have been reports of harm in babies born to women using similar drugs, the risk may not be the same with this drug. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk; however, many doctors consider breastfeeding safe while using this medication. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not contain all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your healthcare professional. Other medications that affect the kidneys or hearing may increase the risk of kidney damage or hearing loss if taken with neomycin. In case of overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., hearing tests, kidney function tests) may be performed while you are taking this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you are taking this drug before scheduled surgery to prevent infection and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, continue with your regular dosing schedule and consult your doctor or pharmacist for a new dosing schedule. If you are taking this drug to treat hepatic encephalopathy and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
